minute-ventilation.short: The volume of air breathed out per minute, in L·min⁻¹: tidal volume × breathing frequency. About 6–9 L·min⁻¹ at rest, about 150 L·min⁻¹ near maximal effort in fit people.

tidal-volume.short: The volume of one breath, in mL or L. About 500 mL at rest; it rises in exercise and often levels off near 3 L at high intensity.

breathing-frequency.short: Breaths per minute. 12–18 at rest in adults, about 50 near maximal effort. It responds within breaths to changes in effort.

alveolar-ventilation.short: The air per minute that reaches the alveoli and takes part in gas exchange: (tidal volume − dead space) × breathing frequency.

partial-pressure.short: The pressure one gas in a mixture exerts on its own: its fraction × the total pressure. Gases diffuse from higher to lower partial pressure. Written PO₂, PCO₂, in mmHg or kPa.

eiah.short: A fall in arterial O₂ during heavy exercise at sea level, seen mostly in highly trained athletes but also in some women of lower fitness. Graded by SaO₂: mild 93–95%, moderate 88–93%, severe below 88%.

central-chemoreceptor.short: A sensor in the brainstem that detects H⁺ in the fluid around it, which rises when blood CO₂ rises, and drives breathing up. The main route by which CO₂ controls breathing.

peripheral-chemoreceptor.short: A sensor in the carotid bodies and the aortic arch that detects blood H⁺, CO₂ and O₂. Its push on breathing for O₂ becomes strong only when arterial PO₂ falls to about 60 mmHg or less.

central-command.short: The feed-forward drive from the brain that activates the working muscles and, at the same time, raises breathing and heart rate. It explains why ventilation jumps the moment exercise starts.

ventilatory-equivalent.short: Litres of air breathed per litre of gas exchanged: V̇E/V̇O₂ for O₂ and V̇E/V̇CO₂ for CO₂. A plain number. Used to find the ventilatory thresholds.

end-tidal.short: The partial pressure of O₂ or CO₂ in the last part of a breath out, measured at the mouth. A non-invasive window on alveolar gas.

vt1.short: The point in a ramp test where V̇E/V̇O₂ and PETO₂ start to rise while V̇E/V̇CO₂ stays flat. It tracks the first lactate threshold.

gas-exchange-threshold.short: The point in a ramp test where CO₂ output starts to rise faster than O₂ uptake. A non-invasive estimate of the lactate threshold, close to VT1.

isocapnic-buffering.short: The stretch of a ramp test between VT1 and the respiratory compensation point, where extra CO₂ from buffering is matched by breathing, so end-tidal PCO₂ stays steady.

respiratory-compensation-point.short: The second ventilatory threshold: V̇E/V̇CO₂ starts to rise and PETCO₂ falls, as breathing outruns CO₂ output to limit the fall in blood pH.

metaboreflex.short: A reflex from fatiguing breathing muscles that raises sympathetic outflow and narrows blood vessels in the limbs, cutting leg blood flow in hard exercise.

rmt.short: Training the breathing muscles by breathing against a resistance (inspiratory muscle training, IMT) or by breathing hard for long spells. It strengthens them and modestly helps performance.
